Decision: keep full tech-stack + data-folder disclosure on About. Reasoning: Vanish has zero network I/O (asserted by test/network-verify.ps1), so exact Electron/Chromium/Node versions and the local data-folder path are never exposed to anyone but the person already sitting at the machine looking at its own About panel - there is no remote attacker this could inform. Matches the project's stated transparency ethos ('never pretends it can do something it cannot'). Not changed: the data-folder line could become a clickable 'reveal in Explorer' action to match Settings' existing set-open-data button, but that is a UX nicety, not a disclosure-risk fix - left for a future pass, not bundled into this one.

De-elevation could not reuse relaunch-elevated's Start-Process -Verb RunAs mechanism: a bare child process launched from an elevated parent INHERITS that elevation (Windows only ADDS privilege via UAC, it never drops it on a plain CreateProcess). scanner.ps1's new relaunch-deelevated action routes through Shell.Application COM instead, which asks the desktop's own explorer.exe to start the process - the standard, documented way to get a process at explorer's own (standard user) integrity from an elevated caller. No UAC prompt is possible or expected on this path, by design: UAC governs requesting MORE privilege, not giving it up.

Implemented: store.elevationAttemptPath() (a JSON marker in the state directory), written by attemptElevatedRelaunch right after Start-Process reports success (main.js), read and ALWAYS deleted on the very next boot's bootstrap sequence regardless of outcome (so a stale marker from a crash or a machine sleeping mid-relaunch can never misfire on a later, unrelated launch). A marker only counts as evidence of the CURRENT boot if it is both present and recent (under 5 minutes old, and not from the future - clock skew guard); if this boot came back non-elevated under those conditions, it is logged to the oplog as relaunch-elevated-mismatch with the full Get-UacDiagnostics snapshot, and surfaced once (get-tier's elevationMismatch field is read-then-cleared, so it shows exactly once, not on every poll) as an explicit toast naming whether UAC appears disabled as a likely cause.

This directly answers the operator's correction: it stops relying on inference from black-box symptoms (app closes, reopens, still shows Audit Mode) and instead gives a definitive yes/no the next time it happens - was this a genuinely-non-elevated relaunch, logged and shown, or (if the diagnostic stays silent on a repeat of the loop) evidence the app never even attempted Start-Process at all, which would point somewhere else entirely.

Verified against the REAL main.js boot sequence (not a mock) in a headless-harness electron process, since this genuinely needed real file I/O and the real bootstrap timing: (1) a marker written ~1s before boot IS detected, logged, returned once via get-tier, and confirmed NOT returned on a second get-tier call in the same session (one-shot); (2) a 10-minutes-stale marker is correctly ignored (no mismatch reported) but still deleted; (3) the marker file is deleted in both cases, proving it can never accumulate or misfire later. Also verified the renderer's toast wiring renders the exact expected text, including the UAC-disabled-likely-cause note, via an offscreen harness.
